workflows.name: Trademark, Copyright & Industrial Design Portfolio Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logos, tagline" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Audit existing IP" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "Establish IP policy and ownership" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-530 (ensure controlled execution — Intellectual Property Portfolio & Brand Protection (PA-100.2).)
- operational: portfolio strategy and audits; operational: assignment clauses
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-protection risk**: Failure to register key marks leaves them vulnerable; mitigated by portfolio strategy and audits
- **Ownership-gap risk**: Ambiguous IP ownership (contractors, vendors) weakens enforcement; mitigated by assignment clauses
System Touchpoints: - IP portfolio docket (W3279); brand/marketing (links to VS-14/VS-41); employment/contracts (links to VS-19/VS-03)

steps.activity: IP Counsel/Marketing (links to VS-14/VS-41) develop IP portfolio strategy: identify protectable assets (word marks, logos, tagline "Your Home Building Partner", private-label brand names, product designs/packaging, marketing creative, software), geographic scope (PH + export markets if applicable), filing priorities, budget; align with brand and private-label strategy

Audit existing IP: inventory registered and unregistered IP, coverage gaps (unprotected marks/creations), renewal status (W3267), infringement exposure (links to VS-71 counterfeits); prioritize protection and cleanup actions

Establish IP policy and ownership: clarify BuildRight ownership of employee/contractor-created IP (work-for-hire, assignment clauses in employment per VS-19 and contractor per VS-98 and vendor per VS-03), use guidelines, brand-usage standards (links to VS-41.3); integrate to brand guidelines

fields.Participants: IP Counsel, IPOPHL Agent/External Counsel, Marketing (links to VS-14/VS-41), Finance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare and file trademark/industrial-design application with IPOPHL" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Manage registration and recordation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-530 (ensure controlled execution — Intellectual Property Portfolio & Brand Protection (PA-100.2).)
- operational: thorough clearance search; operational: experienced counsel
Pain Points / Risks: - **Clearance-miss risk**: Adopting an infringing mark → rebrand cost and liability; mitigated by thorough clearance search
- **Prosecution-failure risk**: Office actions/oppositions unresolved → loss of filing and priority; mitigated by experienced counsel
System Touchpoints: - IP docket/portfolio (W3279); marketing/brand (links to VS-14/VS-41); finance/AP for fees (links to VS-15)

steps.activity: IP Counsel conduct clearance search: search IPOPHL database (and Madrid/international where relevant) for identical/confusingly-similar marks in target classes (hardware/retail — classes 6, 7, 8, 19, 20, 35, etc.); assess registrability and infringement risk; advise on adoptability before launch investment

File and prosecute application: prepare and file trademark/industrial-design application with IPOPHL (Republic Act 8293 IP Code), respond to office actions, manage publication/opposition period, overcome oppositions; coordinate international filings (Madrid Protocol) where applicable

Manage registration and recordation: receive certificate of registration, record in IP portfolio (W3279), set renewal calendar (W3267); coordinate copyright deposit with the National Library where applicable; communicate protected status to Marketing/Merchandising for ® use

fields.Participants: Legal Ops Mgr, IP Counsel, Finance (links to VS-15), IPOPHL Agent
fields.Trigger: Renewal deadline (trademark 10th year + every 10 years per RA 8293); portfolio review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generate renewal reminders with adequate lead time" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "file renewals/DAU with IPOPHL via agent, pay fees" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "records and analytics" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-154 (ensure legal matter & IP portfolio control.)
- operational: docket calendar and lead-time reminders; operational: lifecycle review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapse risk: Missed renewal/DAU → loss of protection; mitigated by docket calendar and lead-time reminders**
- **Waste risk: Renewing unused marks wastes fees; mitigated by lifecycle review**
System Touchpoints: - IP docket/portfolio (W3279); AP/fees (links to VS-15); analytics (W3272)

steps.activity: Legal Ops Mgr maintain IP docket and renewal calendar: track all registrations, renewal dates, grace periods, use-in-commerce requirements (Declaration of Actual Use — DAU per IPOPHL); generate renewal reminders with adequate lead time
Execute renewals and DAU filings: prepare and file renewals/DAU with IPOPHL via agent, pay fees (links to VS-15), submit evidence of use; manage international renewals where applicable
steps.r: IP Counsel / IPOPHL Agent / Legal Ops Mgr

steps.activity: Portfolio lifecycle decisions: at renewal, assess whether mark/IP still in use/strategic — renew, allow to lapse (save cost), or divest; update portfolio records and analytics (W3272); manage IP cleanup
steps.r: Legal Ops Mgr / IP Counsel / Marketing

workflows.name: Domain Name, Anti-Cybersquatting & Digital IP Protection

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-register of "register and renew BuildRight domains" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Monitor for digital IP abuse" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-file of "Enforce against digital abuse" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-530 (ensure controlled execution — Intellectual Property Portfolio & Brand Protection (PA-100.2).)
- operational: monitoring and takedown; operational: defensive registration and UDRP
Pain Points / Risks: - **Phishing/impersonation risk: Fake sites/accounts defraud customers and damage brand; mitigated by monitoring and takedown**
- **Cybersquatting risk: Third parties register brand domains; mitigated by defensive registration and UDRP**
System Touchpoints: - Domain/DNS management (links to VS-27); brand monitoring; security (links to VS-27.3); marketplace (links to VS-95)

steps.activity: Manage domain portfolio: register and renew BuildRight domains (buildright.com.ph and variants, defensive registrations across TLDs, product/campaign domains per VS-75 digital engagement), DNS management, SSL/brand protection; align with brand launches (W3265)

Monitor for digital IP abuse: watch for typosquatting, cybersquatting, impersonating websites, phishing domains, unauthorized social-media handles/accounts (links to VS-14.2), counterfeit listings on marketplaces (links to VS-95); use brand-protection monitoring services

Enforce against digital abuse: send cease-and-desist, file UDRP/URS (via accredited dispute-resolution provider) or IPOPHL cybersquatting action under RA 8293, takedown requests with registrars/platforms/social media, coordinate anti-phishing (links to VS-27.3/VS-86); update analytics (W3272)

fields.Frequency: Recurring brand-abuse class: several confirmed impersonation waves per year across social platforms and marketplace apps (Philippine online-shopping scam prevalence); a wave can spike sharply when a scam listing goes viral
fields.Owner: IP Counsel (event owner); VP Legal & Compliance (enforcement posture)
fields.Participants: Brand/Marketing (VS-14 advisory), Store Operations & service desks (victim-arrival scripts), VS-27.3 (phishing-domain/infrastructure coordination), platform fraud channels & marketplace IP desks, PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group (referral), VS-91 (breach assessment where personal data was harvested), Customer Service (VS-13), Talent Acquisition (W5557's careers-site advisory where the wave touches hiring)
fields.Trigger: Discovery that scammers are impersonating BuildRight to defraud consumers — fake "BuildRight sale/clearance" social-media pages and marketplace listings selling goods the scammers never hold, too-good-to-be-true offers with "pickup at [BuildRight store]", fake promo/raffle pages harvesting personal data, or scam victims arriving at a store demanding goods they "paid" online
fields.Volume: 1 wave × the takedown surface (fake pages, listings, e-wallet handles) × victim contacts arriving at ~200 stores' service desks; the blast radius is brand trust and complaint volume, not inventory — the goods never existed

workflows.name: Brand-Impersonation Commerce-Scam Response (Fake Sellers & Fraudulent Pickup Offers)

Automation Opportunity: - Brand-monitoring alerts routed into a case queue with scam-handle clustering (replaces manual discovery)
- Takedown-request templates per platform with status tracking and escalation timers
- Advisory-banner CMS push to official channels and the store-communication cascade
- Service-desk script distribution with acknowledgment tracking across ~200 stores
Background: 'Fake seller'/'scam listing' appear in zero PA files — W3271/W3272 own the monitoring and takedown machinery, W3268 the infringement action against identifiable abusers, W5557 the recruitment-fraud variant whose victims arrive at BuildRight's own door, and VS-125 watches customer-side payment fraud — nobody owned the commerce-scam event itself: the victims-arrive-at-our-stores protocol (people who paid scammers presenting at a service desk expecting goods), the same-day public advisory with a single verification source of truth, the one-simultaneous-wave takedown discipline, the e-wallet recall guidance and PNP-ACG referral, or the data-harvesting variant that triggers the W53 breach-assessment clock.
Controls: - CTL-530 (ensure controlled execution — Intellectual Property Portfolio & Brand Protection (PA-100.2).)

- operational: evidence preserved before takedown requests are filed; the advisory text approved by Legal before publication; victim-arrival scripts version-controlled and acknowledged by all service desks
Pain Points / Risks: - **Victim-trust risk**: victims blamed or bounced at the service desk becomes the viral story; mitigated by Step 2's empathy-first script and advisory sheet
- **Serialization risk**: takedowns filed one platform at a time let the wave hop surfaces for weeks; mitigated by Step 4's simultaneous-wave discipline
- **Payment-recovery loss**: e-wallet remittances to scammers are rarely recoverable after day one; mitigated by Step 2's same-day recall guidance and the ACG referral
- **Brand-confusion risk**: fake pages outrank official channels in search and social; mitigated by Step 3's verification source of truth and Step 7's discoverability work
- **Recurrence risk**: the same operators re-emerge under new handles; mitigated by the W3271 watch list and Step 7's monitoring tuning
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed by the IP/legal bench, brand team and store service desks; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Brand-protection case record with evidence attachments on the W3271 watch list
- Takedown-request tracking per platform with status and impact notes
- Advisory-banner CMS on official channels and the careers site (links to W3762)
- Store-communication cascade (VS-63) carrying the victim-arrival script
- PNP-ACG/DTI referral evidence pack assembled from the case record
- Breach-assessment intake (links to VS-91/W53) for data-harvesting variants
Time Estimate: Per wave ≈ 20–40 staff-hours across legal, brand and store communications (verification, advisory, takedown wave, referral pack) plus service-desk minutes per victim contact; the several-waves-per-year cadence stays absorbed within the brand-protection, store-communications and service-desk teams.

steps.activity: **Verify & scope**: confirm the accounts/pages are not BuildRight's (cloned logos, typo-squat handles); inventory the takedown surface; preserve evidence — URLs, screenshots, payment trails, victim reports

**Victim-arrival protocol**: service-desk script live chain-wide — victims are treated as customers of a fraud committed against BuildRight's brand: never blamed, given the advisory sheet, guided to the platform report channel, the same-day e-wallet/bank recall request, and the PNP Anti-Cybercrime referral

**Public advisory**: same-day advisory on official channels — BuildRight never sells via personal e-wallets or chat handles; the official store list and the verification page are the single source of truth; no engagement with scammers

**Takedown wave**: one simultaneous multi-surface report wave riding the W3271/W3272 machinery plus platform fraud/IP channels — registrar, marketplaces, social platforms, e-wallet providers — never filed serially
**Law-enforcement & regulatory referral**: evidence pack to the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group; DTI advisory-office coordination where a promo/giveaway scam is widespread
**Data-harvesting variant**: where the fake page harvested personal data (fake raffle/promo forms), route to the W53 breach assessment — the NPC 72-hour clock applies from confirmation
**After-action**: wave post-mortem — verification-page discoverability, service-desk script refresh, platform-relationship notes, and W3271 watch-list tuning for known scammer handles
